title: Signal Skillet — Raw Asks & Implementation Maps (Mar 7 2026)
content:
Purpose
Short working synthesis of recent field feedback (Feb 18–Mar 3 2026) from 8 accounts, support tickets, and CSM interviews. Goal: surface low-risk quick fixes, map higher-effort product work, and suggest runable probes for engineering/product in the next 6 weeks. Not a formal roadmap — working notes.

Context + signals observed (tl;dr)
- Multiple customers report cost surprises tied to burst rounding and unexpectedly long KV cache warms. Notes from infra + billing teams: we see a pattern where infrequent long-context requests cause per-token cost to spike due to cold KV and non-optimal batching.
- Platform users want finer-grained observability per-route + per-request (not just per-token aggregates): token-level timing, which kernel ran, and whether fallback model served.
- Private deployment customers (regulated finance, healthcare) repeatedly asked for KMS key rotation documentation and a small on-prem guide to set up HSM-backed private deployments.
- A few product/AI-native customers want “deterministic canaries”: pin model + quantization variant to canary pods during rollout so outputs and cost metrics are stable for 24–48h before full rollout.
- Ops requests: enable conditional fallback policies that prefer lower-cost model variants when latency is under SLO, else fall back to higher-quality.

Representative quotes (unedited)
- “We had a surprise invoice because some user ran a report with 8k tokens — KV warmed and cost doubled. We need cheaper cold paths.” — finance lead, HealthAI
- “I can’t tell which model actually answered the request when there’s a chain of fallbacks.” — infra engineering, AdTextCo
- “Docs on KMS + HSM would save us a week of back-and-forth with support.” — security engineer, BankEdge

Top themes and short descriptions
1) Observability granularity (high impact, med complexity)
   - Customers need token-level timing per request, kernel identifiers, and explicit fallback labels in traces/logs.
   - Probe: expose a per-request obs-mode (lightweight) that tags served-model-id, fallback-reason, kernel-id and emits aggregated token latency buckets. Run on hosted beta for 3 customers.

2) Cold-path cost smoothing (high impact, high complexity)
   - Problem: KV cache warm is expensive for ad-hoc long-context requests. Requests: cheaper cold paths, pre-warm API, or predictive warm based on user schedule.
   - Ideas: offer an opt-in prewarm hook (customer calls prewarm(session_id, token_prefix)) or token-based budget caps; or async cheaper partial-response mode (initial chunk from smaller context, then full stream).

3) Canary determinism for rollouts (med impact, med complexity)
   - Customers want model+quantization pinning for canary deployments to produce stable evals.
   - Quick experiment: allow a canary flag at route level that forces model variant pin and retains exact KV mapping for 24h. Measure delta on quality/regressions.

4) Private deployment onboarding docs and HSM examples (med impact, low complexity)
   - Deliverable: short-runbook + example terraform snippets for KMS/HSM rotation, minimal network diagrams, and checklist for audit logs.

5) Conditional routing by cost/latency (high impact, high complexity)
   - Customers want routing policies that use cheaper variants when under SLO, escalate if SLO violated.
   - Sketch: extend routing policy language with conditions: if median_latency(route, 1m) < 90% SLO then route->variant-A else variant-B. Also require per-request tag for SLA tier.

Prioritized fixes / proposed owner assignments (quick list)
- Fix A: Add explicit "served_model_id" and "fallback_reason" to existing request trace (hosted). (owner: Marco Ruiz, eng-observability) — low effort, immediate.
- Fix B: Add a billing warning email for >1M token single request and flag on dashboard. (owner: Dana Thompson, product-billing) — low effort.
- Fix C: Create KMS/HSM runbook + Terraform examples document (owner: Lina Chen, solutions-eng) — low effort.
- Fix D: Expose per-route sampling mode that includes kernel id & token latency histogram in logs (owner: Eng Observability, follow Marco) — medium effort.

Suggested experiments / probes (6-week horizon)
- Probe 1 (Observability Beta): 3 customers opt-in to per-request debug traces (sample 1 in 50 by default). Track utility and overhead. Success metric: 75% of incidents resolved faster; perf overhead <5%.
- Probe 2 (Prewarm API alpha): 2 clients try prewarm with controlled schedule for nightly reports. Metric: decrease in cost-per-report by >20% vs baseline.
- Probe 3 (Canary Pin): One pilot route to test canary pinning on a mid-size SaaS customer; measure regression detection rate and false positives.

Customer request catalog (compact, raw)
- HealthAI: cheaper cold path OR prewarm API; invoice anomaly reporting (JIRA-CS-2148).
- AdTextCo: traces showing fallback model id; prefer per-route sampling (slack thread).
- BankEdge: KMS rotation docs; HSM example (customer asked for FIPS 140-2 checklist).
- RetailOps: conditional routing to lower-cost variant for non-critical queries.

Impact vs Effort quick matrix (subjective)
- Low effort / high impact: served_model_id in traces; billing single-request warning; KMS runbook
- Med effort / high impact: per-route obs sampling with kernel ids; canary pin flag
- High effort / high impact: cold-path architecture changes; conditional routing engine

Unresolved questions / risks
- Prewarm API security: who is authorized to prewarm a route? Abuse vector for DoS or cost gaming. Need auth + rate limits.
- Billing UX: how to communicate partial-credits or refunds for surprise invoices? Ops prefers automation but legal ops needs guardrails.
- Metric overhead: token-level histograms could produce a lot of telemetry. Need efficient aggregation and sampling.

Next steps (short)
1) Marco to sketch small trace payload change (served_model_id, fallback_reason, kernel_id) and schedule PR by Mar 15.
2) Lina to draft KMS/HSM runbook and sample terraform by Mar 21; hand to solutions-eng for review.
3) Product + Eng to pick one customer for Prewarm alpha (owner: Dana). Confirm acceptance criteria end of week.
4) Schedule 30m sync with infra, billing, and product to align guardrails for prewarm + billing-warning on Mar 12.

Notes to self / leftovers
- Put a quick FAQ for customers about "why some requests cost more" into the billing docs; link to sample query patterns.
- Consider a small "cold-mode" model variant (lower precision transformer with faster cold starts) as a medium-term product idea.

Appendix: quick links + raw artifacts
- Raw tickets: CS-2121, CS-2148, CS-2153 (long-report invoice)
- Slack threads: #cs-feedback thread ts:1615567384; #infra-kv-warm ts:1615601020
